20.6: while we left Philippi after the Feast of Unleavened Bread, met up with them in five days, and chilled in Troas for a whole week.
20.7: On Sunday, we all got together to break bread. Paul was leavin' the next day, so he preached—and y'all, he kept goin' till midnight.
20.8: The room was lit up with lamps, everybody gathered in this third-floor spot.
20.9: This one young dude named Eutychus was sittin' in the window. He started noddin' off hard, and then BAM—he fell straight out the window from the third floor. Dead.
20.10: Paul ran down, threw himself on the boy and said, "Chill, y'all—he still got life in him."
20.11: Then Paul went back upstairs, ate, talked some more until sunrise (man don't stop), and then finally dipped.
20.12: They brought Eutychus back alive, and everybody was shook—but thankful.
20.13: We went ahead on the boat to Assos, where Paul said he'd meet us—he walked it out instead.
20.14: When he linked back up with us, we boarded and hit Mitylene.
20.15: Next day, we passed Chios, then Samos, stayed a minute in Trogyllium, and then made it to Miletus.
20.16: Paul skipped Ephesus this time—he was on a deadline tryna make it to Jerusalem for Pentecost.
20.17: From Miletus, Paul sent word for the elders in Ephesus to pull up.
20.18: When they got there, he said: "Y'all know how I been livin' since day one—
20.19: I served the Lord humble, with tears, even while folks was out here plottin'.
20.20: I ain't hold back nothin'. I told y'all everything that would help—whether it was out in the streets or inside y'all's homes.
20.21: I told both Jews and Greeks to turn to God and believe in Jesus."
20.22: "Now the Spirit got me headed to Jerusalem, and I don't know what's waiting on me—
20.23: except every city I go, the Holy Spirit keep warnin' me: 'Chains and pain ahead.'
20.24: But I ain't pressed. I just wanna finish my race strong, and do what Jesus told me to—spread the good news of God's grace."
20.25: "Truth is, I know this is goodbye. Ain't none of y'all gon' see me again.
20.26: But I want y'all to know—I ain't got no blood on my hands.
20.27: I gave y'all the whole truth, not just the feel-good parts."
20.28: "So y'all better watch over yourselves and the flock. The Holy Spirit picked y'all to be leaders, to guard God's people—His church, the one He paid for with His own blood.
20.29: 'Cause once I'm gone, some savage wolves gon' pull up and won't care who they hurt.
20.30: Even some of y'all gon' switch up, sayin' wild stuff just to get followers."
20.31: "So stay on alert. Y'all remember—I was out here day and night, cryin' while warnin' folks for three years straight.
20.32: Now I leave y'all in God's hands and in His word, which will build y'all up and give y'all a place with the holy ones.
20.33: I wasn't out here beggin' for y'all's money or clothes.
20.34: Y'all saw me—these hands fed me and my people.
20.35: I was showin' y'all how to grind and help the weak. Remember what Jesus said: 'It's more blessed to give than to receive.'"
20.36: When Paul finished, he dropped to his knees and prayed with 'em all.
20.37: They all cried hard, hugged on him tight, kissed him like family.
20.38: What hit them hardest? He said they'd never see him again. They walked him down to the boat... hearts heavy.

21.1: So after we said our goodbyes, we hit the water and sailed straight to Cos, then the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.
21.2: We found a ship headin' to Phoenicia, hopped on, and kept it movin'.
21.3: We passed Cyprus on our left, made it to Syria, and docked at Tyre so the ship could unload cargo.
21.4: While we was there, we found some disciples and stayed with 'em for a whole week. They kept tellin' Paul through the Spirit, "Don't go to Jerusalem, bruh."
21.5: But once the week was up, we hit the road again. The whole crew—wives, kids and all—walked us out the city. We all got on our knees by the water and prayed together.
21.6: After hugs and goodbyes, we got on the boat. They went back home.
21.7: We finished that leg in Ptolemais, greeted the fam there, and stayed for a day.
21.8: The next day we rolled out to Caesarea and stayed with Philip the Evangelist—yeah, that same Philip from back in the day, one of the Seven.
21.9: Bro had four daughters, all of 'em virgins, and all of 'em prophesying.
21.10: After chillin' there for some days, this prophet named Agabus pulled up from Judea.
21.11: Man grabbed Paul's belt, tied up his own hands and feet with it, and said, "The Holy Spirit say: the dude who owns this belt gon' get bound up like this by the Jews in Jerusalem, and handed over to the Gentiles."
21.12: Soon as we heard that, everybody started beggin' Paul not to go.
21.13: But Paul was like, "Y'all cryin' and breakin' my heart. I ain't just ready to be locked up—I'm ready to die in Jerusalem if it's for Jesus."
21.14: When we saw he wasn't gon' change his mind, we stopped pushin' and just said, "Aight then. Let God's will be done."
21.15: After all that, we packed up and headed to Jerusalem.
21.16: Some of the Caesarea disciples came with us and took us to stay with Mnason from Cyprus—he was one of the OG believers.
21.17: When we got to Jerusalem, the fam welcomed us with open arms.
21.18: The next day, Paul went to go holla at James and the elders.
21.19: He gave the whole rundown—everything God had been doin' among the Gentiles through his ministry.
21.20: They was hyped and praised God. But then they hit Paul with, "Look, bruh… there's mad Jewish believers here, and they real serious about the law.
21.21: Word on the street is you tellin' Jews livin' with Gentiles to forget Moses, stop circumcisin' they kids, and ditch the customs.
21.22: So what we gon' do? Folks already know you in town.
21.23: Here's the move—there's four brothas who done took a vow.
21.24: Go with 'em, get purified too, and cover their expenses so they can do what they need to do. That way, folks will see you still respectin' the law.
21.25: As for the Gentile believers, we already sent word sayin' they don't need to do all that—just stay away from food offered to idols, blood, strangled animals, and sexual sin."
21.26: So Paul did what they said. The next day he purified himself with them and went to the temple, lettin' folks know when the vow time would end and sacrifices would be made for all of them.
21.27: But when the seven days were almost up, some Jews from Asia saw Paul in the temple and started a whole scene.
21.28: "Y'all! This the dude preachin' against our people, our law, and this temple everywhere he go! And now he brought a Greek in here too, defilin' this holy place!"
21.29: (They assumed Paul brought Trophimus in 'cause they saw him earlier in the city.)
21.30: That's all it took. The whole city went wild. Folks grabbed Paul, dragged him out, and slammed the temple doors shut.
21.31: They were tryna kill him when word reached the Roman commander that the city was in chaos.
21.32: He rolled up with some soldiers, and soon as the crowd saw them, they stopped beatin' Paul.
21.33: The commander arrested him, threw on two chains, and started askin', "Who is this man? What he do?"
21.34: But the crowd was yellin' all kinds of different stuff—nobody could give a straight answer. So the commander ordered him to be taken to the barracks.
21.35: The mob was so wild, the soldiers had to carry Paul up the stairs.
21.36: Folks were trailin' behind, shoutin', "GET RID OF HIM!"
21.37: Just as they were about to take him inside, Paul said, "Yo, can I talk to you?" The commander said, "You speak Greek?!
21.38: I thought you was that Egyptian who started that rebellion with 4,000 killers in the wilderness."
21.39: Paul said, "Nah, I'm a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia—real city, not some backwater place. Please, let me talk to the people."
21.40: The commander gave him the green light. So Paul stood on the steps, waved his hand to quiet everybody down, and once it got real silent, he started speakin' to them in Hebrew.

22.1: "Fam, y'all—brothas and fathers—listen up. I'm 'bout to explain myself."
22.2: Soon as they heard Paul speakin' Hebrew, the whole crowd got real quiet.
22.3: He said, "I'm a Jew, born in Tarsus, raised right here in this city. I studied under Gamaliel, got schooled strict in the Law just like y'all. I was deep in it—on fire for God, just like y'all are now.
22.4: I went hard against this Way—had folks locked up, men and women, even had 'em killed.
22.5: The high priest and the elders can vouch for me—I had papers on me from them, went straight to Damascus to snatch up believers and drag 'em back to Jerusalem for punishment."
22.6: "One day around noon, on my way to Damascus, boom—a light from heaven popped off all around me.
22.7: I hit the ground, and I heard a voice say, 'Saul, Saul, why you comin' for Me?'
22.8: I said, 'Who are You, Lord?' And He said, 'I'm Jesus of Nazareth, the one you been goin' after.'
22.9: The folks with me saw the light too—they was shook—but they ain't hear what He told me.
22.10: So I said, 'What You want me to do, Lord?' He said, 'Get up, go to Damascus. You'll get your orders there.'
22.11: I was blinded by that glory light, so the folks with me had to guide me by hand to Damascus."
22.12: "There was this dude named Ananias, solid brother, respected by all the Jews out there, a man of the law.
22.13: He pulled up on me and said, 'Brother Saul, see again.' And just like that, I could see.
22.14: Then he said, 'The God of our ancestors picked you. He want you to know His will, see the Righteous One, and hear His voice.
22.15: You gon' be His witness, tellin' everybody what you saw and heard.
22.16: So what you waitin' on? Get up, get baptized, get them sins washed off, and call on Jesus' name.'"
22.17: "Later on, I came back to Jerusalem and was prayin' in the temple. I caught a vision.
22.18: Jesus told me straight: 'Get outta here quick. These folks ain't gon' listen to what you say about Me.'
22.19: I said, 'Lord, they know how I was—I had Your people beat down and locked up.
22.20: I was right there when Stephen got stoned, noddin' in approval, holdin' the coats for the killers.'
22.21: But Jesus said, 'Leave. I'm sendin' you far off—to the Gentiles.'"
22.22: That was the last straw. The crowd lost it. "Get rid of him! He don't deserve to breathe!"
22.23: They was shoutin', throwin' off they cloaks, flingin' dust in the air like it was a riot.
22.24: The commander was like, "We gotta get this man inside and find out what's up." He ordered Paul to get whooped till he talked.
22.25: But while they was tyin' him up, Paul turned to the centurion and said, "Yo… y'all really gon' beat a Roman citizen who ain't even been found guilty yet?"
22.26: That made the soldier pause. He ran to the commander: "Sir… we gotta be careful. Dude is Roman."
22.27: The commander pulled up and asked Paul, "Is that true? You Roman?" Paul said, "Yeah."
22.28: The commander said, "Man, it cost me a whole bag to get my citizenship." Paul said, "I ain't pay for mine—I was born with it."
22.29: Soon as they heard that, the squad backed up real quick. Even the commander got nervous—he had Paul chained up not knowin' he was Roman.
22.30: The next day, the commander still ain't know why the Jews was goin' so hard on Paul. So he called in the chief priests and the full council. He had Paul brought in, ready to stand before them all.

23.1: Paul locked eyes with the council and said, "Look, fam—I been movin' right with God this whole time. My conscience clean."
23.2: The high priest Ananias wasn't feelin' that and told somebody nearby, "Smack him in the mouth!"
23.3: Paul snapped, "God gon' smack you, bruh. You a fake wall—lookin' holy on the outside but dirty underneath. You sittin' up here actin' like a judge by the law, but then tellin' folks to hit me against the law?"
23.4: The folks near him said, "Yo! You talkin' reckless to God's high priest?"
23.5: Paul said, "My bad, fam—I ain't know he was the high priest. The Word do say, 'Don't bad-mouth your leaders.' I'll respect that."
23.6: Then Paul peeped game: part of the council was Sadducees, part was Pharisees. So he played it smart and said, "Look, y'all—I'm a Pharisee, son of a Pharisee! I'm on trial today 'cause I believe in the resurrection of the dead!"
23.7: Soon as he said that, the room blew up—Pharisees vs. Sadducees went at it.
23.8: (Sadducees don't believe in resurrection, angels, or spirits—Pharisees believe in all that.)
23.9: Folks was shoutin'. Pharisee scribes even said, "We don't see no wrong in this man! What if he really heard from an angel or somethin'? We betta not be fightin' God."
23.10: It got so wild, the commander was scared they'd tear Paul apart. He had the soldiers rush in, grab Paul, and get him outta there back to the barracks.
23.11: That night, Jesus pulled up on Paul and said, "Keep ya head up, Paul. You repped Me in Jerusalem. Now it's time for you to speak on My name in Rome too."
23.12: Next morning, a crew of Jewish men got together, swearin' on everything—they wasn't eatin' or drinkin' till Paul was dead.
23.13: There was more than forty of 'em in the crew.
23.14: They pulled up on the religious leaders and said, "Look, we made a vow. We not touchin' food 'til Paul's gone.
23.15: Y'all need to hit up the commander, act like y'all wanna question him again. We'll be posted up, ready to end him before he even show up."
23.16: Paul's nephew heard the whole thing and ran to the barracks to tell him.
23.17: Paul told a guard, "Take my nephew to the commander. He got somethin' urgent to say."
23.18: The soldier brought the boy in. "Paul, the prisoner, asked me to bring this young man to you. He got a message."
23.19: The commander took the boy aside and said, "What's good? What you gotta tell me?"
23.20: The boy said, "The Jews plannin' to ask you to bring Paul to the council like they wanna question him again. But it's a setup—they tryna kill him.
23.21: Over forty of 'em out there lyin' in wait. They already swore not to eat or drink 'til he gone. Don't fall for it—they ready and just waitin' on your word."
23.22: The commander nodded, "Bet. Keep this between us—don't tell nobody you told me this."
23.23: Right away, he called two centurions: "We movin' out tonight, 9 PM sharp. Get 200 foot soldiers, 70 on horseback, and 200 spear-holders—we takin' Paul to Caesarea.
23.24: Get the man a horse too. We gon' make sure he get there safe to see Governor Felix."
23.26: "From Claudius Lysias, To His Excellency Governor Felix: Respect.
23.27: The Jews tried to kill this man. I pulled up with my squad and rescued him when I found out he was a Roman citizen.
23.28: I wanted to know why they was mad, so I brought him to their council.
23.29: Turns out, it was all about their religious beef—nothin' worthy of jail or death.
23.30: Then I heard there was a plot to kill him, so I'm sendin' him to you now. His accusers can bring their case to you direct. Peace."
23.31: That night, the soldiers followed orders and took Paul to Antipatris.
23.32: The next day, the foot soldiers went back, but the horsemen kept rollin' with Paul.
23.33: They made it to Caesarea, handed the letter to Felix, and presented Paul.
23.34: Felix read it and asked Paul, "Where you from?" Paul said, "Cilicia."
23.35: Felix said, "Aight. I'll hear your case once your accusers pull up." And just like that, Paul got posted up in Herod's Praetorium.

24.1: A few days later, the high priest Ananias showed up with some elders and a smooth-talking lawyer named Tertullus. They pulled up on Governor Felix ready to throw dirt on Paul's name.
24.2: When they brought Paul in, Tertullus kicked off his lil speech: "Your Excellency, Felix—we been real blessed under your rule. You done brought peace and prosperity, and we appreciate that—fr fr.
24.3: Everywhere we go, folks stay grateful. But I ain't tryna waste your time, so let me keep it short.
24.5: This man right here? A straight menace. A walking disease. Stirring up mess among Jews across the globe. He's the ringleader of them Nazarene folks.
24.6: He even tried to disrespect the temple. We caught him, and we was tryna handle it ourselves with our laws—
24.7: but Commander Lysias busted in heavy-handed, snatched him up from us,
24.8: and told us to bring this whole thing to you. You dig into it, you'll see everything we say is true."
24.9: The rest of the Jews in the room nodded like, "Yup. That's facts."
24.10: Felix gave Paul the signal to speak, and Paul said: "Felix, I know you been in this game a long time, so I'm glad to lay my case out in front of you.
24.11: I only been in Jerusalem for twelve days, and all I did was worship.
24.12: Ain't nobody catch me arguing in the temple, starting no riot in the streets or synagogue.
24.13: They can't prove none of what they say.
24.14: But I'ma keep it 💯—yeah, I follow 'The Way' they call a sect. But I worship the same God our ancestors did, and I believe everything written in the Law and the Prophets.
24.15: Just like them, I believe in the resurrection—of both the righteous and the foul.
24.16: So I stay on point, keepin' my conscience clean before God and people."
24.17: "After some years, I came back to bless my folks—bring 'em gifts, do some offerings.
24.18: That's when some Jews from Asia saw me in the temple. I was purified, minding my business—no crowd, no drama.
24.19: But where they at tho? They supposed to be here if they got a problem.
24.20: Or these dudes here—did they catch me doing wrong?
24.21: Only thing I said in front of the council was, 'I'm on trial today 'cause I believe in the resurrection of the dead.' That's it."
24.22: Felix, who actually knew a lil somethin' about "The Way," didn't rule right away. He said, "I'ma wait for Commander Lysias to get here before I decide."
24.23: In the meantime, he told the guards to hold Paul—but give him some freedom. His people could visit and look out for him.
24.24: A few days later, Felix came back with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish. He called for Paul to talk about faith in Christ.
24.25: But when Paul started breaking down righteousness, self-control, and that judgment comin', Felix got real uncomfortable. He was like, "Yeah… we good for now. I'll holler at you later."
24.26: Truth is, he was low-key hoping Paul would offer some money to buy his freedom. So he kept calling him up—talkin', waiting, plotting.
24.27: Two whole years passed. Then Porcius Festus took over for Felix. But before he dipped, Felix left Paul locked up—just to keep the Jews happy.

25.1: So after Festus stepped into power in the province, three days later he pulled up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.
25.2: Soon as he got there, the high priest and top Jewish leaders came to him with beef about Paul.
25.3: They begged him to bring Paul back to Jerusalem—tryin' to play slick, 'cause they had folks ready to ambush him on the road and take him out.
25.4: But Festus shut that down quick. He said, "Nah, Paul stayin' in Caesarea. I'll be back there soon anyway."
25.5: He told 'em, "If y'all really got something to say, roll with me down there and make your case in court."
25.6: After kickin' it in Jerusalem for ten-plus days, Festus headed back to Caesarea. The very next day, he sat up in court and called for Paul.
25.7: When Paul came through, the same Jews that followed him down jumped up with a bunch of serious-sounding lies—but couldn't prove a single one.
25.8: Paul stood firm: "I ain't break no Jewish law, I ain't disrespect the temple, and I definitely ain't come for Caesar."
25.9: But Festus, still tryna earn some brownie points with the Jews, asked, "You wanna go to Jerusalem and stand trial there in front of me?"
25.10: Paul said, "Look, I'm already in the right courtroom—Caesar's. This where I should be judged. You know I ain't do nothin' wrong to the Jews.
25.11: If I did something foul, I ain't afraid to die. But if they lyin'? Ain't nobody handin' me over just 'cause they askin. I appeal to Caesar."
25.12: Festus huddled up with his people, then came back and said, "Aight then—you wanna go to Caesar? To Caesar you go."
25.13: A few days later, King Agrippa and his sister Bernice pulled up to Caesarea to give Festus that royal welcome.
25.14: They kicked it for a while, and Festus brought up Paul's situation. He said, "This dude was left locked up by Felix.
25.15: The Jewish leaders tried to get me to sentence him when I was in Jerusalem.
25.16: But I told 'em, 'Nah, that ain't how Romans roll. A man gotta face his accusers and defend himself.'"
25.17: "So the next day we had court. I expected some wild charges, but nah—
25.18: they just started debating some religious stuff and this man Jesus who supposedly died—but Paul sayin' He alive.
25.20: I ain't know how to handle all that, so I asked Paul if he wanted to go to Jerusalem.
25.21: But he was like, 'Nah, I'm takin' this to Caesar.' So I'm holdin' him 'til I can ship him off."
25.22: Then Agrippa said, "I wanna hear him too." Festus was like, "Bet. Tomorrow."
25.23: So the next day, Agrippa and Bernice walked in like royalty, posted up with the military squad and all the VIPs of the city. Festus gave the word, and Paul was brought in.
25.24: Festus addressed the room: "Y'all see this man right here? The Jews—both in Jerusalem and here—been pressin' me to kill him.
25.25: But I ain't found him guilty of nothing worthy of death. And since he appealed to Caesar, I'm sendin' him.
25.26: Problem is, I don't got nothin' solid to write in the report. So I brought him here, especially for you, King Agrippa, to help me figure this out.
25.27: 'Cause let's be real—it'd be wild to send somebody up to Caesar with no real charges written down."

26.1: King Agrippa told Paul, "Aight, go 'head and speak for yourself." Paul raised his hand like, "Bet," and started in:
26.2: "I'm actually glad I get to talk to you today, King Agrippa, 'cause you know all the Jewish stuff—our customs, our drama. So I'ma need you to rock with me for a bit and really listen.
26.3: You know how I been livin'—everybody do. From when I was a kid in Jerusalem, raised Pharisee-style, hardcore with it.
26.4: If they wanna be real, they can tell you: I was deep in it, followin' the strictest path in the game.
26.5: Now I'm standin' here gettin' judged 'cause I still believe in the promise God made to our ancestors.
26.6: That same promise all twelve tribes been hopin' for while servin' God day and night. That's the whole reason they got beef with me.
26.7: But real talk—why is it so wild to believe God can raise the dead?"
26.8: "I used to be the main one goin' against Jesus.
26.9: I locked folks up, had 'em killed, voted against 'em—straight up villain.
26.10: I ran up in synagogues, had people tortured, forced 'em to speak against Jesus. I was mad hateful, chasin' believers way outta town."
26.11: "But one day, while I was on my way to Damascus with official paperwork from the priests—
26.12: Boom. High noon. Outta nowhere, a light from heaven brighter than the sun lit us all up.
26.13: We hit the ground. Then I heard a voice in Hebrew: 'Saul, Saul, why you comin' for Me? You just hurtin' yourself fightin' Me.'
26.14: I was like, 'Who are You, Lord?'
26.15: The voice said, 'I'm Jesus—the One you been tryna cancel.
26.16: Get up. I got plans for you. You gon' be My messenger—tellin' folks what you seen and what I'ma show you.
26.17: I'ma protect you from both your own people and the Gentiles.
26.18: I'm sendin' you to open they eyes. To pull 'em outta darkness, outta Satan's grip, and bring 'em to God. So they can get forgiveness and get a seat at the table with My people—through faith in Me.'"
26.19: "So yeah, King Agrippa, I ain't play God on that. I got right to it.
26.20: Started preachin' in Damascus, then Jerusalem, then Judea, then out to the Gentiles. Tellin' everybody: Repent. Turn to God. Live right.
26.21: That's why they tried to take me out in the temple.
26.22: But God had me. So I'm still here today, speakin' to everybody—rich or poor, known or unknown.
26.23: And all I'm sayin' is what the prophets and Moses said would happen: That the Christ would suffer, rise up first from the dead, and bring light to both Jews and Gentiles."
26.24: Right as Paul was preachin', Festus shouted, "Paul, you done lost your mind! All that book-learnin' got you tweakin'!"
26.25: Paul said, "Nah, Festus. I'm speakin' facts. Real talk.
26.26: The king knows what I'm talkin' about—ain't none of this been in secret. You feel me, King Agrippa?"
26.27: "You believe the prophets, right? I know you do."
26.28: Agrippa hit him with, "Boy... you almost made me a Christian today."
26.29: Paul said, "Man, I wish you and everybody else in here would really get saved—not just almost. Just like me... minus these chains tho."
26.30: After that, the king, the governor, Bernice, and everybody else dipped out.
26.31: They was talkin' like, "Yo, this dude ain't done nothin' wrong."
26.32: Agrippa told Festus, "He coulda walked free... if he ain't ask to go see Caesar."

27.1: Once they made the call to send us to Italy, they handed Paul and some other prisoners over to a Roman officer named Julius, part of the Augustan Regiment.
27.2: We boarded a ship from Adramyttium, headin' out along the coast of Asia. Aristarchus, a brother from Thessalonica, rolled with us too.
27.3: The next day we docked at Sidon. Julius was cool with Paul and let him go see his people so they could take care of him.
27.4: We left there and sailed near Cyprus 'cause the wind was actin' up.
27.5: Then we passed the waters near Cilicia and Pamphylia, and hit Myra, a city in Lycia.
27.6: There, Julius found a ship from Alexandria headed to Italy, and transferred us on board.
27.7: We moved slow for days, barely makin' it past Cnidus. The wind wasn't lettin' us push forward, so we sailed under the coast of Crete, near Salmone.
27.8: It was a rough ride, but we made it to a spot called Fair Havens, close to Lasea.
27.9: By then, we had already spent too much time at sea. It was late in the season and dangerous to sail. So Paul gave 'em a word:
27.10: "Y'all, I feel like if we push ahead, it's gon' be bad—loss of cargo, the ship, maybe even our lives."
27.11: But the centurion listened more to the pilot and the shipowner than to what Paul was sayin'.
27.12: Since Fair Havens wasn't a good place to spend the winter, most of the crew voted to keep sailin' to Phoenix, another port in Crete that faced southwest and northwest, hoping to chill there for the season.
27.13: When a gentle south wind came through, they thought it was a good time to go. So they pulled out, staying close to Crete.
27.14: But not long after, a violent storm called Euroclydon came down like a beast.
27.15: The ship got caught—we couldn't control it—so we just let the wind take us.
27.16: We ducked under the shelter of a little island called Clauda and barely managed to secure the lifeboat.
27.17: Once we got it on board, they tied ropes under the ship to hold it together. They were scared we'd hit the Syrtis Sands, so they lowered the gear and just let the storm push us.
27.18: The next day, the storm beat us down so hard we started throwin' stuff overboard.
27.19: On day three, we tossed the ship's gear ourselves.
27.20: After days with no sun, no stars—just storm after storm—we started thinkin' all hope was gone.
27.21: Nobody had eaten in days. Paul stood up and said, "Y'all shoulda listened to me and stayed in Crete. Then we wouldn't be out here losin' cargo, almost losin' lives.
27.22: But listen—I'm tellin' y'all now, take heart. Ain't nobody gon' die. We'll lose the ship, but not one soul.
27.23: Last night, an angel from the God I serve and belong to stood by me and said:
27.24: 'Paul, don't be scared. You must stand before Caesar. And God's got you covered—He's sparin' everybody sailin' with you.'
27.25: So take heart, y'all. I believe God. It's gon' happen exactly how He told me.
27.26: But we will crash on some island."
27.27: On the fourteenth night, still gettin' tossed around the Adriatic Sea, the sailors started feelin' like land was close.
27.28: They checked the depth—first 120 feet, then a little later, 90 feet.
27.29: They got scared we'd hit rocks, so they dropped four anchors from the back of the ship and prayed for daylight.
27.30: Some of the sailors tried to sneak off in the lifeboat, pretending they were setting anchors from the front.
27.31: But Paul told the centurion and soldiers, "If those men leave this ship, y'all not gon' make it."
27.32: So the soldiers cut the ropes and let the lifeboat drop.
27.33: Just before sunrise, Paul told everybody, "Y'all been fasting for 14 days, scared and not eatin'.
27.34: But I need y'all to eat somethin' now—it's for your survival. Ain't even a hair on your head gon' be lost."
27.35: Then he took bread, gave thanks to God in front of everybody, broke it, and started eatin'.
27.36: That lifted everybody's spirits, and they ate too.
27.37: Altogether, there were 276 people on that ship.
27.38: After they had enough to eat, they lightened the load by throwin' the wheat cargo into the sea.
27.39: When daylight hit, they didn't recognize the land but saw a bay with a beach. So they aimed to run the ship aground there.
27.40: They cut the anchors, let 'em drop, untied the rudder ropes, raised the sail, and aimed for the beach.
27.41: But they hit a spot where two seas came together, and the ship got stuck. The front end jammed up and wouldn't move, and the back end got torn apart by the waves.
27.42: The soldiers wanted to kill the prisoners so none of them could escape.
27.43: But the centurion, tryin' to save Paul, stopped them. He told the ones who could swim to jump in first and make it to land.
27.44: The rest grabbed onto broken pieces of the ship. And just like that, every single one of them made it safely to shore.

28.1: Once we made it out safe, we found out the island was called Malta.
28.2: The locals showed us mad love—built a fire and welcomed everybody, since it was cold and rainin'.
28.3: Paul was helpin'—gathered some sticks for the fire. But as soon as he threw the bundle in, a snake jumped out from the heat and latched on to his hand!
28.4: The islanders saw it hangin' and said, "Oh yeah, this man guilty for real. He survived the sea, but karma—aka 'justice'—still gon' get him."
28.5: But Paul? He just shook that snake off into the fire like it was nothin'. Didn't even flinch.
28.6: They waited, watchin' like, "He 'bout to swell up or drop dead." But after a while with no symptoms, they switched up like folks do—"Oh snap, he must be a god!"
28.7: Not too far from there was the house of a man named Publius, the top dude on the island. He hosted us for three days with real hospitality.
28.8: Turns out, Publius's father was layin' sick with fever and stomach issues. Paul pulled up, prayed, laid hands on him—and he got healed.
28.9: Word spread. Then everybody on the island who was sick came through—and they all got healed too.
28.10: They showed us so much love, honored us in all kinds of ways. When we got ready to leave, they made sure we had everything we needed.
28.11: Three months later, we left on a ship from Alexandria that had wintered there. It had the Twin Brothers carved on the front.
28.12: We stopped at Syracuse and stayed three days.
28.13: From there, we made our way to Rhegium. The next day the south wind kicked in, and we arrived in Puteoli.
28.14: We found some believers there who invited us to stay a whole week. Then we made our way toward Rome.
28.15: When the believers in Rome heard we were comin', they pulled up to meet us at Appii Forum and Three Inns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and felt encouraged.
28.16: Once we got to Rome, the centurion handed the other prisoners over to the guards, but Paul? He got some freedom—allowed to live by himself with just one soldier watchin' him.
28.17: After three days, Paul called a meeting with the Jewish leaders in Rome. When they came through, he said: "Fam, I didn't do nothin' against our people or traditions, but I still got handed over to the Romans in chains.
28.18: When they investigated, they wanted to let me go—there was no reason to execute me.
28.19: But the Jews kept pushin', so I had to appeal to Caesar. Not to snitch on my people—but to defend myself.
28.20: That's why I called y'all here today. I'm locked up right now, wearin' this chain—for the hope of Israel."
28.21: They told him, "We ain't heard nothin' from Judea about you. Nobody here brought charges.
28.22: But we do wanna hear what you think, 'cause everybody been talkin' wild about this group you represent."
28.23: So they set up a day to come hear Paul out. When they showed up at his spot, Paul broke it all the way down—talked about the kingdom of God, showed how Jesus fulfilled the Law and the Prophets, taught from morning 'til evening.
28.24: Some folks were feelin' it, some were still doubting.
28.25: But when they couldn't agree, Paul hit them with this: "The Holy Spirit told y'all truth through Isaiah when He said:
28.26: 'Go tell the people: You'll listen, but won't really hear. You'll look, but won't really see.
28.27: Their hearts dull, ears closed, eyes shut. They don't wanna turn around and be healed.'"
28.28: "So just know this: God's salvation is goin' to the Gentiles now— and they gon' listen."
28.29: After he said that, the Jews left arguin' among themselves.
28.30: Paul stayed two whole years in his own rented place. The door stayed open—anybody who wanted the truth could pull up.
28.31: He kept preachin' the kingdom of God and teachin' about Jesus Christ, bold and unbothered—nobody stoppin' him.
